A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Q-UCRL study of infinite-horizon average-reward reinforcement learning, despite changes to the title, authors and formatting. All main sections, equations, figures and Appendices A–B are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports an algorithm and theoretical regret analysis, with convexity and quantum-computing background in the appendices. Its references to quantum experiments concern oracle operations, not reported experimental outcomes.

after.justification: v2 adds theoretical estimation bounds and revises the regret theorem, but reports no original experiments, simulations or data analyses in either the main text or appendices.

M1.justification: v1 Eq. (24) applies quantum mean estimation to accumulated quantum samples. v2 Eqs. (21)–(25) instead estimate from the latest completed epoch and combine that estimate with the previous estimate using visitation-count weights. This substantially changes transition estimation to avoid reusing measured quantum samples, while retaining optimistic policy optimization.

E1.justification: Neither version actually trains or evaluates on datasets, benchmarks or instantiated test environments. The theoretical infinite-horizon average-reward task remains the same.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods experimentally. Classical RL and quantum-bandit algorithms appear as theoretical context and related work.

E3.justification: Neither version reports an empirical evaluation protocol. Changes to quantum sample handling and analytical confidence bounds concern the method and theory.

E4.justification: Neither version contains ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies or empirical case analyses. Appendices A–B retain the convexity argument and amplitude-amplification overview.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated empirical runs, seeds, error bars or statistical tests. The revised probabilistic estimation guarantees are theoretical results, assessed under T1.

E6.justification: Neither version reports concrete empirical scores, rankings or observed findings. The changed analytical regret guarantee is assessed under T1.

T1.justification: v2 adds a quantum sampling-oracle definition and Lemmas 2–3 analyzing quantum-query overhead and accumulated error from combining epoch estimates. These changes propagate through the transition-error and regret proofs. Theorem 1 changes from O(S^3 A^2 T_mix log^2(S^2 A T)) in v1 to O(S^5 A^4 T_mix log^(11/2)(S^2 A T) log log(T)) in v2. The mixing-time and known-reward assumptions and both appendices remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: v2's introduction adds a contribution claim for transition estimation that explicitly accounts for measurement-induced quantum state collapse. The headline claims of polylogarithmic regret, improvement over classical square-root dependence on T, and novelty for infinite-horizon average-reward MDPs remain.

C2.justification: v2 newly explains that measurement destroys reusable quantum samples and motivates retaining classical estimates across epochs instead. This adds a substantive operational constraint and mechanism explanation. The existing limitation to model-based methods and proposed model-free extension remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 Algorithm 1 explicitly initializes transition estimates and records epoch starting times; Eq. (25) specifies the time interval and state-action filtering defining each estimation batch. These add concrete bookkeeping details. Neither version supplies code, hardware specifications or measured runtimes.

R1.justification: v2 adds supporting references for sampling oracles and quantum foundations, including Sidford and Zhang, Nielsen and Chuang, and additional quantum-RL work. Section IV also contrasts one-time quantum sample use with classical approaches. The broader positioning against bandits, discounted RL and episodic RL remains.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title and author information, adds a quantum-computing basics subsection, and locally rewrites the oracle and estimation explanations. The overall six-section narrative and appendix organization remain, with much existing prose retained.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reformatted from one column to two columns, changing equation, algorithm and appendix layouts. Figure 1 is redrawn to separate the quantum transition oracle from the classical MDP environment, with revised connections, labels and caption. Both appendices are retained in the condensed layout.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses v1's reuse of quantum samples through epoch-specific estimation and adds explicit oracle and query-cost analysis. However, v2 retains the old confidence radius in Eq. (20), while its new Lemma 3 introduces a larger estimation-error bound containing an epoch-dependent factor eC. The PDF does not reconcile this with the optimism argument in Eq. (58). The clearer method and analysis therefore coexist with an unresolved justification of the central regret guarantee, preventing a reliable overall quality judgment.
